globalRelease.label: Pre-release hardening
globalRelease.summary: SparkEngine is source-usable and feature-rich, but it is not yet a fully ready engine release. Required CI can mask failures, no versioned release exists, shipping artifacts are not signed or attested, and the stable-v1 Windows, D3D11, editor, NullRHI, installed-package, public-SDK, and SparkGameFPS evidence is not certified.
definition: Every declared release profile is ready at the same source commit; each profile's required gates are passing and its applicable work is complete.
Required builds and tests fail closed and attach machine-readable evidence.
Primary platform, renderer, editor, packaged runtime, and SDK workflows pass end to end.
Every advertised game module meets its declared release profile or is explicitly labeled as a prototype/template.
Versioned Shipping artifacts are reproducible, signed, checksummed, scanned, attested, installable, uninstallable, and rollback-tested.
Security, performance, crash recovery, compatibility, documentation, legal, and operations gates have named evidence and owners.
The repository-generated site bundle and handoff match the exact tested commit.

statusPromotionRules: Implementation, verification, support, and release are independent dimensions; never infer one from another.
A capability cannot be release-ready while a required gate is not passing or a blocking work item is open.
Global release readiness is derived from every declared release profile; gates explicitly excluded by every profile may remain blocked and must stay labeled unsupported or experimental.
Every work item explicitly classifies its applicability to every release profile as required, shared, or outside, and no profile may depend transitively on outside work.

A release profile's declared build products are its supported surface: required and shared products are both blocking, so a configuration report may not be clean while any of them is missing, mis-kinded, or unevidenced; only build options may be classified outside.
A passing test must execute production source or a packaged binary; mirror-only, tautological, or mock-only tests cannot promote readiness.
Every public numeric claim resolves through a generated metric with an evidence path.
Every readiness promotion includes source, tests, CI evidence, documentation, limitations, and website impact in the same change.
Production-ready wording is forbidden until the global release state is ready at the displayed commit.
If live publication fails, the website labels the last valid bundle stale or unavailable; it never silently calls the fallback current.

releaseProfiles.name: Stable v1
releaseProfiles.summary: The single product shape SparkEngine intends to declare stable first: a Windows 11 x64 host built with the MSVC v143 toolset line, rendering through Direct3D 11 with NullRHI as the headless path, gameplay authored in C++ game modules, and delivered as one installed first-party single-player vertical slice, SparkGameFPS, that must build through the public SDK surface alone. Constrained LAN play is optional and is not required. Every capability outside this profile is experimental or unsupported and must never be framed as a supported release surface. Nothing in this profile is certified while its state is blocked.

scope.label: Host operating system
scope.value: Windows 11 x64 only. Windows 10 x64 and every non-Windows host remain documented development and build floors; they are outside this profile and are not certified by it.

evidence.label: Pinned x64 Windows build and test lane
Declared Windows minimum and recommended host

scope.label: Supported compiler line
scope.value: The MSVC v143 toolset line (Visual Studio 17 2022 generator, architecture x64, toolset v143). The exact MSVC compiler build and Windows SDK version are not pinned yet, so this names the supported line, not a certified toolchain.

evidence.label: Configure step pins the Visual Studio 17 2022 generator with -A x64 -T v143
windows-debug, windows-release, windows-shipping, and windows-development presets pin toolset v143

scope.label: Headless path
scope.value: NullRHI on Windows 11 x64: the no-render device path for GPU-less execution and automation. NullRHI renders nothing. It is not software rendering, and the llvmpipe software OpenGL path belongs to the experimental OpenGL backend outside this profile.

scope.label: Gameplay authoring language
scope.value: C++23 game modules built against the SDK module interface

scope.label: First-party game
scope.value: SparkGameFPS, one first-party single-player vertical slice that must build through the public SDK surface alone. Constrained LAN play is optional and is not required by this profile.

evidence.label: Current build reaches into SparkEngineLib and the engine source tree; the public-API-only requirement is unmet
Public SDK surface the slice must build against

scope.label: Delivered product shape
scope.value: One installed single-player vertical slice authored in SparkEditor, cooked, packaged, installed, and run without external services

conflatedTerms.reason: NullRHI is a no-render device that rasterizes nothing. Software rasterization through Mesa llvmpipe is the experimental OpenGL path and is outside this profile, so the two must never be described as the same thing.

excludedGates.reason: Scripting is outside the profile: AngelScript and visual scripting are declared experimental and no profile claim depends on them.
The profile is single-player and service-free, so production multiplayer transport and online services are out of scope and declared experimental or unsupported.

limitations: Windows 11 client-host certification does not exist; the build-windows-vs2022 lane runs on the hosted windows-2022 image, so host certification remains PLT-200 work rather than published evidence.
No Shipping-configuration artifact is signed, checksummed, attested, installed, upgraded, or rollback-tested at a single commit.
The first-party slice SparkGameFPS is in the profile but uncertified: its release state is blocked and it holds this profile at blocked (MOD-310).
SparkGameFPS builds against SparkEngineLib with the engine source tree on its include path, so the public-API-only requirement is unmet (SDK-240, MOD-310).
No exact MSVC compiler build or Windows SDK version is pinned; the hosted windows-2022 image floats, so the toolchain is neither reproducible nor certified (BLD-100, PLT-200, CI-120).
The editor-to-cook-to-package-to-install-to-run loop has no same-commit end-to-end certification.
MSVC v145 and Visual Studio 2026 are an advisory continue-on-error lane, not a supported compiler line in this profile.
Windows 10 x64 and the Linux and macOS build floors stay documented as development minima, but this profile certifies only Windows 11 x64; headless execution is in profile only on that same host.

Breadth is frozen: this profile inherits no work that exists only for out-of-profile capabilities. Linux, macOS, D3D12, Vulkan, OpenGL, Metal, multiplayer transport, production service operations, and the prototype modules keep their own open work outside this gate and stay uncertified.

rules: Start only work items whose dependencies are done; parallelize every independent item in the same wave.
Keep implementation, production-source tests, documentation, readiness status, generated handoff, and website impact in one change.
Do not close an item from comments or screenshots alone; execute its commands and attach exact-SHA CI evidence.
If acceptance reveals a new blocker, add a stable work-item ID and dependency before expanding scope.
Never weaken a gate to make it pass. Fix the implementation, evidence path, or public claim.
At the end of each session, regenerate the handoff and leave the first unblocked item explicit.
